main_text.p: per affusionem novæ aquæ regiæ, donec os Leonis rubei (ut appellitant) probè referatum sit, quod in digestione positum circulatur, postea abstracta aqua ascendit spiritus Mercurialis. In hoc supra præparatum vitriolum primo solvitur & digeritur donec fæculentiam omnem deposuit. Hæc aqua oleaginea solvit supra præparatum sulphur in duplà sui proportione. His tribus partibus quatuor astri Mercurialis addunt & sic in balneo per dies 40. digerunt, donec in viridem ac viscosum liquorem abeant omnia, quæ postmodò in furno Physico lenissimè coagulantur in Medicinam fixam. Alii viam siccam sequentes mineram ab auro separant, aurumq; spiritu suo inpregnatum leniter contusum per retortam

page.notes: The text is set in a single column within a decorative border. The catchword and signature are not visible. The word "affusionem" and some letters in "Leonis" and "referatum" are slightly blurred in the scan; the transcription follows the visible letters. The line-end "fæculentiam" and "siccam" carry a printed hyphen-like mark (a tail on the m/ n) that is read as a line-end sign, not a hyphen, and is left unhyphenated.
